title: Chick Webb: encouragement and his unreachable conception
summary: Chick Webb's band stood opposite Teddy Hill's; Webb encouraged him, and Clarke says he could copy Webb's technique but never his conception.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, what did -- tell me something. Did you and Chick ever talk?
Oh, we played on the bandstand opposite each other.
With Edgar Hayes, or --
No, with Teddy Hill.
Oh.
Chick was on the left bandstand and we were on the right.
Yeah, that's right. That's right.
So every time, when we would finish, well I would be sitting behind Chick.
Well, Chick didn't -- he didn't -- he dug what you were doing, didn't he?

Oh, he always told me. He would come out to the fair and say, 'Kid, you're making great progress. You're doing fine, kid. Keep it up.' He would always encourage me. In the Savoy he said, 'Gee, what was that tune you just played?' You know? Although --
Oh, no, he was sincere.
I know he was, because I was --
Because he would say just the opposite if he meant it.
I was so close to him, you know, and why he liked me, God only knows. I guess, like I say, God has always been with me, all my life.
Well, the think about Chick was, I mean anybody that played he loved them. Whatever they played,
Yeah. I remember --
He was a guy that -- you know, music was everything to him.
That's right. That's right. That's what -- that was his life.
That was his life.
You know?
Well, tell me something, what kind of a drummer was he, then?
Oh, Chick -- I can't describe Chick.
Yeah. I know him so well. I want to hear what you think about it.
He was so fantastic, because I knew that I would never be able to play like Chick.
How come?
His conception. Not his technique and all.
No, no.
Because I could always copy his technique.
Sure. Sure, yeah.
But the way he played, I could never reach that stage. His conceptions, the way he would do things.
Throw himself in it. Project it.
Yeah. I could never do that. So --
Because that was his personality.
That was him. That was Chick.
Yeah.
And all I could do was enjoy it and try to get as much out of it as I could.
You got a thrill out of it.
Oh, my God, I would stay behind him all day, all night. All night long I was there. 'Hey, where's Kenny?' There I'd be, sitting behind Chick. That's where I was.
